small_guidance:
- M=128 is tiny; BLOCK_M=128 means only 1 row-tile, killing the GROUP_M swizzle and limiting grid parallelism to N/BLOCK_N (~64-128 programs). Add configs with BLOCK_M=64 or 32 (e.g. 64x256x32, 32x256x64, 64x128x64) so more SMs are utilized; also try BLOCK_N=256 with BLOCK_K=128.
- K=16384 is huge — add num_stages=4-5 configs with BLOCK_K=64/128 to better overlap global loads with `tl.dot`; drop BLOCK_K=32 entries since they pay more loop overhead.
- Mark `M`, `N`, `K` divisibility hints via `tl.multiple_of`/`tl.max_contiguous` on the load pointers, and drop the per-iteration bounds masking (K is divisible by BLOCK_K here) so the inner loop compiles to pure unmasked loads.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a split-K (or stream-K) GEMM: with M=128 the grid is bottlenecked on N-tiles, but K=16384 has tons of work — partition K across programs and atomic-add (or two-stage reduce) into the output, then apply bias/min/sub in a tiny epilogue kernel. This unlocks all 128 SMs of the 4090.
- Alternatively, design a persistent kernel with BLOCK_M=128 (covering all rows in one tile-row) and one program per N-tile; each program walks K in long stages with double/triple buffering. This removes the GROUP_M swizzle (irrelevant at M=128) and maximizes K-loop pipelining.
- Keep weight in its native [N,K] layout and load with K contiguous (no pre-transpose copy) — current `weight_t.contiguous()` costs a 1 GB copy on every weight version change; load B as `w_ptr + offs_n[None,:]*K + offs_k[:,None]` directly, or pre-pack once into a registered buffer at init.
